title: MV Help me to use SRD skill extender plugin

posts.author: donghoy
posts.body:
Hi, I'm a newbie who enjoy making a game.
I have a problem with SRD skill extender plugin.
I wrote commend <Extend Skills: 2, 3, 4> in a note tag of skill 1.
Then, when I clicked skill 1 in the skill window, skill 2, 3 and 4 are displayed in the sub skill window. It worked well.
HOWEVER, the skill 2, 3 and 4 are displayed with skill 1 in the skill window too!
This problem occurs also in a battle.
Why are the extended skills in skill 1 remained in the skill window?!
I couldn't find a case like mine yet.
Maybe this problem occurs only for me
Please help me to use this useful plugin.

posts.author: ATT_Turan
posts.body:
donghoy said:
Is there anything I'm misunderstanding and doing wrong?
Click to expand...
No. I don't see any code in the plugin that prevents a contained skill from also showing up in the regular skill list.
I would consider it a glaring design flaw, but you aren't doing anything wrong.
You could see if someone's interested in making an extension/patch for the plugin, or you could work around it.
With Yanfly's Skill Core installed, you can give the contained skill the notetag:
Code:
<Custom Show Eval>
visible = SceneManager._scene instanceof Scene_Battle && SceneManager._scene._skillExtend.isOpen();
</Custom Show Eval>
And that should hide it from your regular list, but show it in the skill extend window.

in a latter portion of the video he showed how he did it, and it suggests that there wasnt code to automatically hide skills that are part of another skill's extend list.
He had the skilltype for "fire" be "Magic", and then changed the skilltypes for all the other fire spells so that they wouldnt show up in the "Magic" list. its the same idea as when i said
Robro33 said:
you could... give those skills an entirely different skilltype that that actor cannot use
Click to expand...
when an actor learns a skill, they still have it learned even if they cant use the skill's skilltype. even if you dont have the skilltype, the extend window will show it. The tag you mentioned will prevent a skill that isnt learned from showing up in the list
This means in general you can have the extended skills be of some skilltype the class doesnt use to hide it from the skill type list, and in the case of having to learn the skills, you can have the class learn the skills as it levels up and have those skills absent from the skilltype list by by making them of some inaccessible skilltype. they still be usable from the extend window when you use the note tag.
